subject: scene-courtyard-pixel
label: Courtyard pixel sample — comparison against the painted plate
notes: This is a DECISION ARTIFACT, not production art. It exists so Raheem can see a pixel courtyard beside the painted one, with the same hero in both, and choose by eye.

TILES CANNOT BE STYLE-ANCHORED TO A CHARACTER. For /create-tiles-pro, style_images defines the tile SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS — the docs are explicit that tile_type/tile_size/tile_view are ignored when it is supplied. Passing the 59x146 hero crop would produce 59x146 'tiles'. So tiles rely on description + outline_mode + tile_view instead, and register match is steered by wording.

OBJECTS CAN be style-anchored, and are. Note the output size is derived from the largest style image, and that size caps how many objects one call returns (<=85 -> 8, <=170 -> 4, else 1). The hero crop is 146px, so ONE call returns up to 4 objects via item_descriptions — cheaper than one call each.
Never anchor anything to courtyard.png. Using the painted plate as a colour reference already cost the hero his face contrast.
View consistency is the subtle killer: the hero was generated at 'low top-down', so tiles use tile_view 'low top-down' and objects use 'top-down'. A mismatch reads as wrong without being nameable.
